transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, good afternoon, sir! Welcome to the shop. I'm afraid Master Tailor is away on business—won't be back for several weeks. Can I help you with something in his absence?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I had ordered a custom-made suit from you two months ago, but I have yet to receive it. I thought it would be ready by now.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Oh, yes, I recall your order, Mr. Lincoln. The tailor did mention it before he left. He said it was completed and picked up just last week. Are you certain you haven't received it?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Yes, I am quite certain. I believe I have paid the appropriate amount for this suit, and I expect it to be delivered as per our agreement. I trust you have fulfilled your responsibilities as my tailor?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I understand your concern, sir. But I have the ledger here—it shows the suit was marked as "collected" on the 15th. Perhaps there was a mix-up? In any case, the tailor is away and won't return for weeks, so I can't ask him directly.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I appreciate your attempt to resolve this, but I'm afraid I cannot wait weeks for a suit that was promised to me months ago. If you can't provide the suit as stated, I will need to take this matter elsewhere. Good day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Sir, I must be clear—all custom orders are final upon pickup. The receipt you signed states clearly that no alterations or refunds are given once the garment leaves the shop. I'm afraid there's nothing I can do while the tailor is away.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Very well then, I will accept that fact. But when I next visit Springfield, I shall expect to see this suit, properly tailored, as I had paid for. And if it is not, I shall expect some satisfactory explanation for your breach of contract. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I will certainly pass along your message when the tailor returns, Mr. Lincoln. I hope the matter can be resolved to your satisfaction then. Good day to you, sir.
